analysis: The supplied units are base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (base lines 2465-3234). The PR's only change per file_changes is a documentation-only insertion at head lines 3541-3575, a new section 'Cluster service listeners follow the cable and the pairing'. That range is not in the supplied base units and its patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the full added text or any source changes. I examined the base context for security-relevant claims the new section would sit beside: cluster pairing, owner-authenticated control channel, encrypted JACCL data plane, sanitized owner-launch environment, and per-tenant prefix partitions (T-041 and its salt scoping). The patch describes a service listener that refuses handshakes keyed with a different pairing and restarts with a changed pairing, comparing pins, label, link epoch and edge but not the edge secret. As documentation of existing behavior this does not weaken any retained control. No code changes are visible, so no concrete regression is demonstrable. Open questions for integration, which are not findings: (1) whether the described listener restart logic (ClusterService.listenerChange, 5 s check interval) actually keeps the pairing-key handshake refusal for stale pairings; (2) whether Pairing.Identity excluding the edge secret from comparison could let a listener keep running under a rotated secret. Neither can be verified from the supplied docs-only evidence. The coordinator-to-provider trust model, App Attest authorization, attestation and the prefix cache threats (T-041) are unaffected by this docs change.
